FundedNext to FNmarkets: 30% Deposit Bonus
FundedNext to FNmarkets: 30% Deposit Bonus
October 20, 2026

Turn your FundedNext Performance Reward into extra trading power. When you route a FundedNext Performance Reward into FNmarkets, you receive a 30% deposit bonus on FNmarkets.

What is 30% Performance Reward Deposit Bonus?

The 30% Performance Reward Deposit Bonus is a promotion where FNmarkets grants you additional trading credit when you move a Performance Reward from FundedNext into FNmarkets.

The bonus equals 30% of the net amount received by FNmarkets (after the FundedNext-side deduction).

It is added as Credit, usable as an additional margin for trading.

It applies to every qualifying transfer while the program is active.

Eligibility for the 30% Performance Reward Deposit Bonus?

The Bonus Program is available to fully verified clients who route funds into FNmarkets via the FundedNext Performance Reward to FNmarkets deposit feature and who meet all the requirements described as follows:

Only funds that are transferred to FNmarkets through the FundedNext Performance Reward deposit feature qualify for this bonus.

You must have completed verified KYC before claiming the bonus in both FundedNext and FNmarkets.

All FNmarkets campaign credits must be linked to a single Standard account, and only that account can receive the Bonus. If the client already has a Standard account tied to another FNmarkets campaign, the FundedNext Performance Reward must be sent to the same account to qualify. If no Standard account exists, the client must open one, after which it will appear as Performance Reward transfer option.

Traders who are banned, blacklisted, or otherwise excluded from any FNmarkets campaign are not eligible.

Bonuses may be withheld or reversed during any ongoing KYC, AML, sanctions, source-of-funds, source-of-wealth, or fraud-prevention review.

How is the bonus calculated under the 30% Performance Reward Deposit Bonus?

A 3.5% withdrawal commission fee is deducted when a Performance Reward is routed to FNmarkets, so the bonus is calculated on the net received amount.

Example: $100 from FundedNext → USD 96.50 received after the 3.5% deduction → bonus = 30% × 96.50 = USD 28.95.

The bonus is credited automatically to the selected Standard account, typically within 24 hours of the transfer.

Limited-Time Offer — Zero Transfer Fees

For a limited time, the 3.5% processing fee is fully waived on FundedNext Performance Reward transfers to FNmarkets. During this campaign, 100% of your payout reaches your FNmarkets Standard account, and your 30% bonus is calculated on that full amount — nothing is deducted.

What are the minimum and maximum limits for the 30% Performance Reward Deposit Bonus?

Minimum: USD 50 (gross, before deduction) sent from the FundedNext Performance Reward. After the deduction, roughly USD 48.25 is received, and the 30% bonus on that is USD 14.48.

Maximum: The most Bonus Credit you can hold at any one time is USD 3,000. Once you hold the USD 3,000 maximum, no further bonus is issued until Credit headroom frees up (for example, after a withdrawal reduces existing Credit).

Examples of how the 30% Performance Reward Deposit Bonus works.
Example 1 — Single Performance Reward transfer

You route a FundedNext Performance Reward of USD 1,000.

After the 3.5% deduction, USD 965 is received into the Standard account.

Bonus = 30% × 965 = USD 289.50.

Total trading equity: USD 1,254.50.

The bonus is calculated on the received USD 965, not the USD 1,000 sent.

Example 2 — Pre-existing Standard account balance

Your Standard account already holds USD 100.

You route a Performance Reward directly to that Standard account; USD 96.50 is received after the 3.5% deduction.

The account balance becomes USD 196.50.

Bonus = 30% × 96.50 = USD 28.95.

Only the FundedNext-sourced USD 96.50 earns the bonus; the pre-existing USD 100 does not.

Limited-Time Offer — Zero Transfer Fees

For a limited time, the 3.5% processing fee is fully waived on FundedNext Performance Reward transfers to FNmarkets. During this campaign, 100% of your payout reaches your FNmarkets Standard account nothing is deducted.

Example 3 — Multiple transfers reaching the cap

First transfer: USD 5,000 received → 30% bonus = USD 1,500.

Second transfer: USD 5,000 received → 30% bonus = USD 1,500.

Total Bonus Credit held: USD 3,000.

You now hold the maximum Bonus Credit and will not receive further bonus on additional transfers until Bonus Credit headroom becomes available again.

Example 4 — Single transfer exceeding the cap

You route a Performance Reward; USD 12,000 is received.

30% of USD 12,000 = USD 3,600.

Since the maximum Bonus Credit is USD 3,000, only USD 3,000 is credited as bonus.

Which countries are excluded from the 30% Performance Reward Deposit Bonus?

The promotion is not available to residents of Hong Kong, Japan, Italy, Uzbekistan, Romania, Taiwan, Singapore, Vietnam, China, Indonesia, and Thailand, or any other jurisdiction where such promotions are restricted or prohibited by law. Eligibility is also subject to FNmarkets' live/banned-country list.

What conduct can disqualify me from the 30% Performance Reward Deposit Bonus?

Any suspected arbitrage, abuse, manipulation, cash-back arbitrage, circular or back-and-forth routing of funds between FundedNext and FNmarkets solely to harvest the bonus, or any fraudulent activity makes a client ineligible. FNmarkets may close affected accounts, suspend participation in this or future promotions, cancel or reverse orders, and result in annual profits or losses.

For any further queries and clarification, please contact FNmarkets support - https://fnmarkets.com/contact-us

This offer is not available to residents of Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Italy, Uzbekistan, Romania, Taiwan, Singapore, or any jurisdiction where such promotions are restricted or prohibited by law.

What Are the Trading Hours in FundedNext Futures?
September 30, 2026

TL;DR: FundedNext Futures does not allow overnight or weekend trade holding. You must close all positions by 3:10 PM Central Time (CT) each trading day — any positions left open are automatically closed at that time. Trading resumes daily at 5:00 PM CT, and after the weekend it resumes on Sunday at 5:00 PM CT. These hours apply to both your Challenge Account during the Challenge Phase and your FundedNext Account.

What are the permitted trading hours at FundedNext Futures?

You can trade each day from 5:00 PM CT, when the new session opens, up until 3:10 PM CT the following day, when all positions must be closed. After the weekend break, trading resumes on Sunday at 5:00 PM CT.

 

FundedNext Futures does not permit overnight or weekend trade holding, so every position must be closed within the daily trading window.

 

What happens if I don't close my trade?

Any positions still open at 3:10 PM CT will be automatically closed. This means you don't need to worry about unintentionally breaching your account by leaving a trade open past the daily close.

 

Note: Avoid repeatedly forcing a trade after the market has closed. In some cases the order may still go through, which can lead to a breach of your account.

 

Can I trade right at the 5:00 PM CT open, and will I get filled?

Yes — you can trade as soon as the session opens at 5:00 PM CT. However, please note that even during the Challenge Phase or on a funded FundedNext Account, we don't recommend trading when the market is illiquid, as this can cause issues with your position, such as slippage or partial fills.

 

Illiquid hours are open for trading, but entirely at the trader's own discretion. The same applies to holiday trading hours.

 

Trading during holiday hours

Holiday trading hours — including any early market closes and the handling of open positions — will be communicated to traders in advance.

Always check the permitted trading times ahead of holidays.

During holiday sessions, be sure to close your own positions before the market closes, as automatic closure may not apply at an early (half-day) close unless you are notified otherwise.

Failure to close positions before the market closes may result in a breach of your account.

I just passed my Challenge Account — what happens next?
I just passed my Challenge Account — what happens next?
September 30, 2026

TL;DR: After you hit your profit target, your Challenge Account isn't upgraded instantly — your results are validated at the end of the trading day. If all pass criteria are met, an agreement pop-up appears on your FundedNext Dashboard; once you sign it, your FundedNext Account is issued. Note that you can have a maximum of 5 active FundedNext Accounts at once and up to 10 issued per month — if you're at that limit, your account stays pending until a slot frees up.

Congratulations on passing your Challenge Account! Reaching your profit target while following the rules is a major milestone. Here's exactly what happens between passing and receiving your FundedNext Account.

 

Do I get my FundedNext Account immediately after passing?

Not right away. When you reach your profit target, your account still needs to go through an end-of-day validation. Because rules like the Maximum Loss Limit and the Consistency Rule are assessed on an End-of-Day (EOD) basis, your results are confirmed after the trading day closes — not the moment you hit your target.

 

This means you should wait until the end of the day for your pass to be processed.

 

What happens at the end of the day?

At the end of the trading day, FundedNext Futures reviews your account to confirm that all pass criteria have been met — including your profit target, the Consistency Rule (where applicable to your model), the Maximum Loss Limit, and all trading rules.

If everything checks out, an agreement pop-up will appear on your FundedNext Dashboard.

 

What if I don't meet all the criteria at the end of the day?

If your account doesn't meet all the pass criteria during the end-of-day validation, the pass will not be processed and no agreement pop-up will appear. Your account simply continues in the Challenge Phase, and you can keep trading toward your target while following the rules.

 

How do I receive my FundedNext Account?

Once the agreement pop-up appears:

Review the agreement shown on your FundedNext Dashboard.

Sign the agreement to accept the terms of your FundedNext Account.

FundedNext Futures — Most Frequently Asked Questions
FundedNext Futures — Most Frequently Asked Questions
Updated over 2 weeks ago

TL;DR: Quick answers to the questions traders ask most. FundedNext Futures charges a one-time fee only (no subscription or activation fee), does not allow overnight or weekend holding, and allows VPN/VPS, news trading, and EAs/bots. There's no daily profit limit, no refunds, no account merging, and no account pause option.

Do I have to pay a monthly subscription fee or activation fee?

At FundedNext Futures, the payment structure is transparent and simple, ensuring traders can focus on trading without an activation fee after completing the challenge. 

No Monthly Subscription Fees: You are not required to pay recurring fees for maintaining a Challenge or FundedNext Account.

One-Time Fee Only: A single fee is paid at the start when you purchase a Challenge.

Free Transition: Moving from a Challenge to a FundedNext Account involves no additional cost.

At FundedNext Futures, your only cost is the initial Challenge fee. Once paid, there are no surprise charges or hidden fees—just trading opportunities and rewards.

 

🔗 See: How to pay for your FundedNext Futures Challenge? 

 

Does FundedNext Futures allow overnight and weekend trade holding?

No. Overnight and weekend holding is not permitted. All positions must be closed by 3:10 PM CT each trading day, and any open positions are closed automatically at that time. Trading resumes at 5:00 PM CT (and Sunday at 5:00 PM CT after the weekend).

 

Why is this policy in place for FundedNext Futures?

Risk Management: Overnight holding or weekend holding exposes traders to potential gap risks when the market reopens.

Account Protection: Automatic liquidation prevents traders from incurring unintended losses due to price fluctuations outside trading hours.

Stable Trading Environment: Ensures all traders operate under the same risk-controlled conditions.

Trader's Responsibility: It is the trader’s responsibility to monitor their positions and ensure they are closed before the designated market closes each day.

 

🔗 See: What are the trading hours in FundedNext Futures?

 

Can I use a VPN/VPS to trade?

Yes. You may use a VPS (Virtual Private Server) or VPN (Virtual Private Network) while trading on both your Challenge Account and your FundedNext Account. 

 

Please note that if inconsistent IP activity is detected in your trading multiple times, our team may reach out to you to request additional documents.

 

Is there a maximum profit limit per day?

No. There is no limit to how much profit you can make in a day. However, where the Consistency Rule applies, you'll need to keep track of your daily profit to ensure a single day doesn't exceed the allowed percentage of your overall total — this is about maintaining consistency, not capping your earnings.

 

🔗 See: Is there any consistency rule to be followed in the FundedNext Futures Challenge & FundedNext Account?

 

Are there any news trading rules?

No — FundedNext Futures does not restrict news trading. That said, trading during news can be risky: the market can move very rapidly, and your Stop Loss may not be respected at your intended price due to sudden price movement.

 

Is there any margin requirement?

In FundedNext Futures, the margin mechanism does not apply in either the Challenge or FundedNext Account. Instead of margin requirements, trading is managed through contract limits.

 

Traders are not required to deposit their own funds or maintain an initial margin to trade with FundedNext. By paying a small fee, they can trade up to the allocated contract limits based on the account size. It is essential to trade within the allowed contracts and adhere to the loss limits.

 

For more details, please visit the following article on the FundedNext Futures contract policy.

 

🔗 What is the contract limit policy at FundedNext Futures?

 

Is the use of Automated Trading Systems (EAs and Bots) allowed?

At FundedNext Futures, you are allowed to use automated trading systems such as Expert Advisors (EAs) and trading bots during both the Challenge and on FundedNext Accounts.

 

However, we do not offer any support for setting up, configuring, or troubleshooting these systems. Any issues—such as technical errors, execution delays, or system malfunctions—must be managed on your own. FundedNext will not be held responsible for any impact these may have on your trading account.

 

Please remember that while the use of EAs and bots is permitted, strategies that aim to exploit system vulnerabilities are strictly prohibited. To ensure a fair and transparent trading environment, the following guidelines apply for eligible accounts:

Traders are required to customize their EA or bot settings to align with their unique trading styles.

Each EA or bot is required to employ a distinct strategy, avoiding identical trades across other traders accounts within FundedNext.

Using an EA that incorporates third-party applications such as Telegram or WhatsApp is strictly prohibited.

Using an EA for latency abuse or order flooding is strictly prohibited.

 

What is the Refund Policy?

At FundedNext Futures, payments are final. Whether you purchase or reset a Challenge, the fees are non-refundable under all circumstances.

 

Why are refunds not possible at FundedNext Futures?

Immediate Costs: As soon as a payment is made, FundedNext incurs costs by paying platforms such as Tradovate or NinjaTrader for account setup.

Irreversible Processing: Due to these upfront expenses, transactions cannot be reversed or refunded.

We strongly recommend that traders carefully review their Challenge selection, account type, and size before completing a purchase.

 

Does FundedNext allow account merging?

Due to the nature of Futures trading, account merging is not supported in FundedNext Futures. Each account operates independently and must be managed separately by the trader. 

 

Can I pause my Futures Challenge or FundedNext Accounts?

No. There is no account pause option at FundedNext Futures — accounts cannot be paused during either the Challenge Phase or the FundedNext Account stage.

 

Is there any Age Restriction to joining FundedNext Futures?

There is an age restriction for joining FundedNext Futures. Traders must be at least 18 years old to open a FundedNext Futures simulated trading account, as futures trading involves financial risk and requires meeting legal and contractual requirements.

How to calculate PnL in Futures trading?
How to calculate PnL in Futures trading?
September 30, 2026

TL;DR: In futures trading, your profit or loss is calculated as (Tick Value × Number of Ticks Moved) × Number of Contracts. The more ticks the price moves in your favor and the more contracts you trade, the greater your profit or loss potential.

In FundedNext Futures calculating Profit and Loss (PnL) is one of the most important skills. Because futures contracts move in fixed tick sizes, every price change directly affects your balance. Understanding how tick size, tick value, and the number of contracts work together lets you accurately measure risk and Performance Reward — so you can plan trades with confidence and avoid surprises.

 

Understanding the key concepts

Before calculating profit or loss, you'll need to understand these core terms:

Tick Size: The smallest possible price movement allowed for a futures contract. It differs across contracts.

Tick Value: The monetary amount gained or lost when the price moves by one tick.

Number of Ticks: The total movement in ticks between your entry and exit price.

Number of Contracts: How many contracts you're trading. More contracts amplify both profits and losses.

Once these basics are clear, you can calculate PnL manually or use a futures profit calculator.

 

What is a tick in futures trading?

A tick is the minimum price change for a futures contract. Prices move in fixed steps, with no smaller increments possible.

 

Example: If the tick size is 0.25 points, the price moves in increments of 0.25 (6000.00 → 6000.25 → 6000.50). Prices will not change by smaller amounts such as 6000.10.

 

Each tick has a tick value, showing the money gained or lost per tick, per contract. 

 

For example, the E-mini S&P 500 futures contract has a tick value of $12.50.

 

How to calculate profit and loss using ticks

Formula:

 

Profit/Loss = (Tick Value × Number of Ticks Moved) × Number of Contracts

 

Example 1 — One contract

You trade 1 contract of the E-mini S&P 500 futures, and the price moves 5 ticks in your favor (6000.00 → 6001.25).

Tick Size: 0.25 points

Tick Value: $12.50

Number of Ticks: 5

Calculation:

 

 5 ticks × $12.50 = $62.50 profit

 

Example 2 — Multiple contracts

You trade 3 contracts of the E-mini S&P 500 futures, and the price moves 5 ticks in your favor.

Tick Size: 0.25 points

Tick Value: $12.50

Number of Ticks: 5

Contracts Traded: 3

Calculation:

 

 (5 ticks × $12.50) × 3 contracts = $62.50 × 3 = $187.50 profit

 

Key points to remember

A tick is the smallest price movement in a futures contract.

Tick size is how much the price can move in one step; tick value is how much money you make or lose per tick.

The more ticks the price moves in your favor, the higher your profit.

The number of contracts multiplies your profit or loss.

If the price moves against you, the same calculation applies to your loss.

TL;DR: A futures instrument code is a standardized shorthand used globally to identify a contract's asset, expiration month, and year. Most codes follow the format: [Root Symbol] + [Month Code] + [Year Code]. For example, in the code GCM5, "GC" represents the asset (Gold), "M" stands for the expiration month (June), and "5" indicates the year (2025). If you see a code starting with an additional "M," such as MGCM5, it denotes a Micro contract.

Every futures contract has a unique instrument code. These codes may look confusing at first, but they are standardized worldwide. Learning to read them is essential for futures traders, as the code instantly tells you what asset is being traded, when the contract expires, and in which year the contract applies.

 

What is a futures instrument code?

A futures instrument code is a short name that tells you:

What asset are you trading (like gold, oil, or the S&P 500)?

Which month does the contract expire?

What year does the contract apply to?

How to read a futures code?

Futures codes usually follow this format:

[Root Instrument Code] + [Month Code] + [Year Code]

Let’s understand this with a real example: GCM5

GC = Root code for Gold

M = Month code for June

5 = Year code for 2025

So, GCM5 refers to the Gold Futures contract that expires in June 2025.

For micro contracts, an additional “M” is included at the beginning of the code.

For example, MGCM5 = Micro Gold contract expiring in June 2025.

 

 

Futures Instrument Month Codes

Futures use a single letter to represent each month:

 

 

While the letters may seem randomly assigned, this is primarily because many of the earlier letters are already associated with specific trading terms. For example, A = Ask, B = Bid, C = Corn, E = Eggs, O = Oats, S = Soybeans, W = Wheat, etc. As a result, the remaining letters are used to represent the months of the year in futures codes.

 

We recommend focusing on the "front-month" contracts, as they tend to be the most actively traded and provide better liquidity.

What is the difference between level 1 and level 2 market data in Futures?
What is the difference between level 1 and level 2 market data in Futures?
September 30, 2026

TL;DR: Level 1 market data provides real-time pricing, including best bid, best ask, and last traded price, and is sufficient for real-time charts when the subscription is active. Level 2 market data does not reduce chart delay and instead provides full order book depth, mainly used for order flow and Depth of Market (DOM) analysis.

Level 1 market data provides real-time pricing information such as the best bid price, best ask price, and the most recent traded price. When a user has an active Level 1 market data subscription through Tradovate, the price charts are not delayed. Any chart delay typically occurs only when a required market data subscription is missing or inactive, not because the user is on Level 1 instead of Level 2.

 

Level 2 market data does not reduce chart delay or make charts more “real-time” compared to Level 1. Instead, Level 2 data provides additional depth by showing the full order book, including multiple bid and ask levels with available quantities at each price. This data is primarily used by traders who rely on order flow analysis or Depth of Market (DOM) for execution decisions.

 

In summary, Level 2 market data is not required to avoid delayed charts. It is an optional enhancement for traders who want deeper visibility into market liquidity, while Level 1 market data is sufficient for real-time charts and standard trading activity when properly subscribed and active.

 

How do I subscribe to Level 2 market data?

Level 2 market data subscription is not sold or managed by FundedNext. It is provided directly by Tradovate within their trading platform. To subscribe to Level 2 market data, log in to your Tradovate dashboard and navigate to the Market Data Subscriptions section. From there, you can select the relevant exchanges and Level 2 data packages and activate the subscription directly through Tradovate.

 

All pricing, billing, and activation of market data subscriptions are handled entirely by Tradovate, and FundedNext does not have visibility or control over these subscriptions.

The following images show the sections in Tradovate where you can subscribe to Level 2 market data. Please note that the images also include a “Cancel Renewal” button. The cancellation steps are explained later on this page.

 

Step 1:

Sign in to the Tradovate web or desktop app.

 

Step 2:

Click Application Settings (slider-bars icon, top-right). Then open Subscriptions.

 

 

Step 3:

Scroll to Market Data and select the exchange(s) you need (CME, CBOT, NYMEX, COMEX, EUREX, etc.).

 

 

 

 

Step 4:

Click Subscribe or Update Subscription, accept terms, and complete payment.

 

 

 

 

Important: After completing the purchase, log out of your Tradovate dashboard and log back in to ensure your Level 2 subscription is activated properly.

 

Step 5:

Verify activation: In Settings → Subscriptions → Market Data, you’ll see your active Level 2 entitlements.

Open a SuperDOM for a symbol on that exchange; you should now see depth beyond best bid/ask.

 

How do I cancel my Level 2 market data subscription?

Cancellation of Level 2 market data subscriptions must be done directly through your Tradovate account. After logging in to the Tradovate dashboard, you can access the Market Data Subscriptions section and manage or cancel your active subscriptions from there.

 

FundedNext is unable to cancel, modify, or manage market data subscriptions on behalf of users, as these services are controlled exclusively by Tradovate.

 

Can I get a refund for my Level 2 market data subscription?

FundedNext cannot provide refunds for Level 2 market data subscription purchases. Since the subscription is purchased directly from Tradovate and billed under Tradovate’s systems, it falls entirely under Tradovate’s subscription and refund policies.

 

If you have questions regarding refunds, billing issues, or subscription disputes related to market data, you must contact Tradovate Support directly, as they are the only party authorized to review or process such requests.

What are the Clarity Cards, and how do they affect my account?
What are the Clarity Cards, and how do they affect my account?
September 30, 2026

TL;DR: Clarity Cards are live tracking tools available directly in your account dashboard. Each card monitors a specific trading parameter in real time, showing you exactly where you stand against the applicable thresholds before any Performance Reward decision is made. The cards update after every trade closes, giving you full visibility into your trading activity at every point in your cycle.

Accessing the Clarity Cards

On your account dashboard, you will find the Clarity Cards displayed alongside your Trading Objective. Each card is specific to your account type and phase. The cards visible to you will depend on whether you hold a Challenge Account or a FundedNext Account.

 

 

Which parameters are visible on the Clarity Cards?

Micro-Scalping Trades: Traders will be able to see all the trades that have been flagged for micro-scalping from this card. The micro-scalping parameter is applicable for the Challenge Account and the FundedNext Account.

 

This card tracks trades that are opened and closed within 10 seconds, showing what percentage of your total recorded profit came from these trades. Only profitable micro scalping trades count toward this percentage; losses from trades closed within 10 seconds are not included.

 

 

What you see on the card:

On your micro-scalping Clarity Card, you will see the following:

Micro-Scalped Trades: The total count of profitable positions opened and closed within 10 seconds.

Micro-Scalped Profit (%): The percentage of your total recorded profit generated from these trades. Keep this below 40%.

Profit from Micro-Scalping ($): The dollar amount generated from these trades.

See Trade Details: A full list of every trade that was categorized as "micro scalping."

Thresholds and consequences:

Challenge Account

At 30%: A compliance warning is issued. No action is taken on the account at this stage.

At 40% or above: Advancement toward the profit target is placed on hold. The account remains active, and trading can continue, but advancement will not be processed until the micro-scalping percentage falls back below 40%. Eligibility is restored automatically once the threshold is cleared.

FundedNext Account

At 30%: A compliance warning is issued to notify the trader of a rule breach or policy concern. At this stage, no deductions, penalties are imposed, and the account remains fully active. The warning serves as an advisory measure, allowing the trader to review and adjust their trading practices to ensure continued compliance with FundedNext's rules and requirements.

At 40% or above: Once micro-scalping profit reaches or exceeds 40%, the micro-scalping portion of profit for that cycle is deducted in full. The account remains active; micro-scalping does not result in account termination at any level on a FundedNext Futures Account. Any future profit attributed to micro-scalping activity will be subject to the same deduction on an ongoing basis.

Checking this card regularly ensures you are aware of your micro-scalping status before your Performance Reward is processed. To learn more, refer to this article here.

 

To learn more about the risk limit rules, please review this article.

Is there any inactivity period in FundedNext Futures?
Is there any inactivity period in FundedNext Futures?
October 12, 2026

TL;DR: FundedNext Futures has an inactivity period. Both FundedNext Challenge and FundedNext Account are breached after 30 consecutive calendar days of no trades. For Futures Direct Account only, the inactivity period is for 7 calendar days. Inactivity count starts if no trade is placed by 04:01:00 PM CT after purchase on the same day, It counts calendar days including weekends, and the timer resets when at least one trade is placed.

FundedNext Futures will deem an account as "inactive" if there is no trading activity within the specified inactivity period:

Challenge Accounts: Marked as breached and deactivated after 30 consecutive calendar days of no trades.

FundedNext Accounts: Marked as inactive and deactivated after 30 consecutive calendar days of no trades.

Direct Accounts: Marked as inactive and deactivated after 7 consecutive calendar days of no trades.

Inactive accounts will be deactivated to maintain platform stability. To avoid this, simply place at least one trade within the respective timeframe. This helps maintain platform stability.

 

How is the inactivity counted?

From the day the Challenge is purchased, if no trades are placed by 04:01:00 PM CT, the inactivity day count begins.

Calendar days are counted (including weekends)

Placing at least one trade resets the inactivity counter

The inactivity count increases each day at 04:01:00 PM CT. Once 30 consecutive inactive days are reached, the account is breached at 04:01:00 PM CT.

 

The inactivity count increases each day at 04:01:00 PM CT. Once 7 consecutive inactive days are reached, the account is breached at 04:01:00 PM CT. (Direct Account only)

 

What happens after the days of inactivity?

The account will be considered breached due to exceeding the futures inactivity period.

Once breached, the account will be deactivated, and trading access will be lost.

If you wish to continue trading, you must reset your account to regain access.

FundedNext Accounts can not be reset; a new purchase is required to continue trading.

Inactive accounts can cause system inefficiencies and may impact the overall trading experience for active users. Keeping your account active ensures smooth platform performance and uninterrupted access to trading features on FundedNext Futures.

How does KYC Verification work at FundedNext?
How does KYC Verification work at FundedNext?
September 30, 2026

TL;DR: KYC is required before your first Performance Reward withdrawal — not before trading. The flow is: Pass Challenge → Sign Agreement → trade your FundedNext Account → complete KYC before withdrawing. Submit a valid photo ID and complete a live selfie; verification typically takes 24–48 hours. KYC is profile-level, so you verify once and it covers all your accounts. All information must be accurate and belong to you — misconduct or multiple-person involvement is a serious violation.

KYC (Know Your Customer) verification is a mandatory step for compliance and security at FundedNext Futures. With recent updates, you can start trading your FundedNext Account without completing KYC immediately — but you must complete it before you can withdraw your first Performance Reward.

 

When is KYC required?

You can trade your FundedNext Account right after passing, but KYC must be approved before your first Performance Reward withdrawal. Simply submitting documents isn't enough — your status must show "Verified." While your KYC is "Required" or "Pending Review," you can keep trading, but you cannot receive a Performance Reward until verification succeeds.

 

What is profile-level KYC?

KYC is maintained at the profile level — a single source of truth for each trader. Once your profile is verified, it applies to every account you hold, across both FundedNext Futures and FundedNext CFD products, so you never need to repeat it for new accounts.

 

The "First-Trigger" Rule: if you hold both Futures and CFD accounts, whichever KYC trigger happens first establishes the verified record for your entire profile. Once approved, no separate KYC is needed for other products or future accounts.

 

Step-by-step: how to complete KYC

Step 1 — Pass the Challenge & sign the agreement. Once you pass while following all trading rules, a notification appears on your dashboard prompting you to sign the FundedNext Agreement in the Verification Center. After signing, you receive your FundedNext Account and can begin trading right away.

 

Step 2 — Start KYC before withdrawal. To withdraw your first Performance Reward, complete KYC. A notification prompts you to begin — click "Verify Now" in the Verification Center of your profile.

 

Step 3 — Choose your verification method. On the Verification Center page, click "Start Verification." You can scan the QR code or receive a verification link via SMS, then follow the link to upload your documents.

 

Step 4 — Submit your ID and complete the liveness check. Provide one valid photo ID (see below), and complete a Liveness Check — a real-time selfie confirming it's really you.

 

Step 5 — Wait for review. Your documents go under review, which typically takes 24–48 hours. You'll be notified in the Verification Center once you're verified — at which point you're eligible to withdraw your first Performance Reward.

 

Which documents do I need?

Provide one valid photo ID:

National ID (government-issued, showing nationality)

Passport

Permanent Residence Permit

Driving License (accepted only for traders in the U.S., Australia, Canada, and New Zealand)

Proof of address (if requested)

In some cases you may be asked to complete address verification via a separate secure link. Acceptable documents:

Utility Bill

Bank Statement

The document must have been issued within the last three months.

 

How many submission attempts do I get?

You get 3 attempts to submit your documents correctly. If you exhaust your attempts, contact our 24/7 Support Team and we'll guide you accordingly.

 

What are the requirements for KYC submissions?

All information and documents you submit must be accurate, current, and belong to you as the account holder. FundedNext reviews every submission to confirm it aligns with your identity and account records.

 

What is a Verification or Compliance Session?

As part of KYC review, FundedNext may request a Verification or Compliance Session to confirm your identity and clarify the information you provided. The following conduct during this process may result in enforcement action:

Providing misinformation or documents that don't belong to the account holder

Failing to give a satisfactory explanation for your information, documents, or trading activity

Attempting to bypass the session

Seeking external assistance during the session

Failing to follow the session guidelines

What are the identity and registration integrity rules?

Every account you open — along with all registration and verification details tied to it — must be entirely your own. Using another person's information (such as an email address or identification details) during registration or KYC is a serious violation of FundedNext's policies. Any indication that more than one individual is involved in setting up or verifying an account is treated as a serious breach, subject to the same enforcement actions.

 

What enforcement actions can FundedNext take?

Depending on the nature of the violation, one or more of the following may apply:

Account Termination

Permanent Termination from the Platform

Performance Reward Ineligibility or Adjustment

Refund Ineligibility

What if I fail or have trouble with KYC?

Failure to complete KYC means you won't be eligible to receive your Performance Reward until it's successfully completed. If you run into any difficulty, reach out to our 24/7 Support Team for guidance.

 

Trading CFDs as well?

Because KYC is profile-level, your verification also covers your FundedNext CFD accounts. For CFD-specific KYC details, see the CFD guide.

Can Multiple Traders Use the Same Wallet Address?
October 2, 2026

TLDR: No. Each trader must register a unique withdrawal wallet address, and an address already registered or used by another trader cannot be used, regardless of the relationship between the individuals. A shared wallet address is treated as a compliance concern and triggers a review under FundedNext's Terms of Service. A first instance results in a formal warning and a required wallet update. A subsequent instance results in Account Termination or Suspension from the Platform, with the Performance Reward or Refund denied or adjusted.

Each trader on FundedNext is required to register a unique wallet address for withdrawals. A wallet address registered or used by another trader on the platform cannot be used, regardless of the relationship between the individuals involved.

 

Where the same wallet address is detected across multiple accounts, FundedNext treats this as a serious compliance concern that triggers a review under its Terms of Service.

 

Why This Rule Exists

A shared wallet address across multiple accounts creates material compliance risks, including potential indicators of money laundering, fraud, or coordinated misuse of the platform. FundedNext is required to identify and act on these risks as part of its ongoing compliance obligations.

 

Enforcement

The enforcement action applied depends on whether a shared wallet address is detected for the first time or on a subsequent occasion.

Violation

	

Enforcement Action




First Instance

	

FundedNext will issue a formal warning. The trader must discontinue use of the shared wallet address and register a unique address not registered by any other trader on the platform. The Performance Reward will be issued only after a compliant wallet address has been registered.




Subsequent Instance

	

Account Termination or Suspension from the Platform. The Performance Reward or Refund will be denied or adjusted.

What Counts as a Subsequent Instance?

A subsequent instance is triggered if, after receiving a formal warning, the trader is found using the same wallet address—or any other wallet address already registered by another trader on the platform. The restriction applies to all shared wallet addresses, not only the one identified in the original warning.

The FundedNext Futures Direct Account is the most direct path to funded trading. Instead of passing a Challenge first, you start on a FundedNext Account immediately at a lower price, with no profit goal. Here's everything that governs the account.

Is there a Consistency Rule on the FundedNext Futures Direct Account?

Yes. The FundedNext Futures Direct Account uses a 20% Perpetual Consistency Rule that tracks your all-time best trading day across every trading cycle.

 

The rule in one line: your highest single-day profit ever recorded on the account may not exceed 20% of your current cycle's total profit.

 

In plain terms, your best trading day ever must stay at 20% or less of what you’ve earned in your active cycle. To check, take your highest day profit and ask: is it 20% or less of this cycle’s total? If yes, you’re consistent and eligible to withdraw.

 

How it works across cycles:

Set your mark (first cycle): Keep your best single day at 20% or less of your total cycle profit. Spread your gains rather than relying on one big session.

Keep your mark (later cycles): Your best day carries forward after your first withdrawal. In each new cycle, keep that figure at 20% or less of the new cycle’s profit.

Raise your mark anytime: A bigger day simply becomes your new all-time best. You’re never penalized for a strong session — just keep that new figure at 20% or less of your cycle profit going forward.

Examples:

Cycle 1 — setting the baseline. Your highest day is $500. For it to sit at 20% of the total, your cycle total must reach at least $2,500.

 

 Days: $500 + $450 + $400 + $350 + $500 + $300 = $2,500 → consistency met. ✅ That $500 day becomes your all-time record.

 

Cycle 2 — the record is maintained. You never beat $500, so the minimum total stays $2,500.

 

 Days: $500 + $400 + $300 + $450 + $500 + $350 = $2,500 → eligible. ✅

 

Cycle 3 — the record is broken. You book a $600 day — a new all-time best. For $600 to sit at 20%, the total must reach $3,000.

 

 Days: $600 + $500 + $500 + $500 + $500 + $400 = $3,000 → eligible. ✅ From now on, $3,000 is the minimum for every future cycle, until an even bigger day is recorded.

What is the Perpetual Consistency Rule and how does it work?
October 7, 2026

TL;DR: The Perpetual Consistency Rule keeps your profits steady rather than reliant on one big day. The rule is simple: your highest single trading day ever recorded on the account must stay at 20% or less of your current cycle's total profit. What makes it perpetual is that your best-day record carries forward across every withdrawal cycle — it stays with you until you beat it, at which point the new, bigger day becomes your record.

What is the Perpetual Consistency Rule?

The Perpetual Consistency Rule is a Performance Reward condition on the FundedNext Futures Direct Account. It requires that your profits come from consistent, repeatable trading rather than a single outsized session.

In one line: your best-ever trading day on the account can't be more than 20% of your current cycle's total profit (a cycle being the period since your last withdrawal or since the account started).

 

The word "perpetual" is what sets this rule apart. On most models, a consistency rule looks only at the cycle directly in front of it. Here, your highest trading day is remembered throughout the account's lifespan. Once you record a best day, that figure follows you from cycle to cycle and becomes the number every future cycle is measured against — until you record an even bigger day, which then becomes your new benchmark.

 

Importantly, you're always in control of this rule. You're never penalized for having a strong day; a bigger day simply raises your benchmark. And because a growing cycle total makes any single day a smaller percentage of the whole, staying compliant becomes easier the longer you trade steadily.

 

How does the Perpetual Consistency Rule work?

To check whether any cycle is consistent, take your highest recorded day and ask a single question: is it 20% or less of the cycle's total profit? If your total is high enough that your best day fits under that 20% ceiling, the cycle is consistent.

Your total profit must be large enough that your highest day profit lands at exactly 20% or less of it — which means your cycle total profit must be at least 5× your best day.

 

For example, a $500 best day needs a cycle total of at least $2,500 ($500 ÷ $2,500 = 20%) to be consistent.

For a $600 day to sit at 20% of the total, the total must reach $3,000 ($600 is 20% of $3,000). The cycle hits exactly $3,000, so consistency is met. 

 

A bigger day isn't free: the new $600 record raises your minimum from $2,500 to $3,000, and that $3,000 minimum now applies to every cycle going forward, until an even bigger day is recorded and resets the benchmark again.

 

How the rule works in your favor

The Perpetual Consistency Rule is designed to reward steady, repeatable trading, and it tends to fade into the background for consistent traders over time. Because your best day becomes a smaller share of your total as you keep earning, the more you trade consistently, the less the rule constrains you. You're never punished for a strong session — a new personal best simply becomes your new mark to maintain.

What is the FundedNext Futures Legacy Challenge?

It evaluates your ability to earn consistent profits while managing risk in a simulated futures environment during the Challenge Phase. Once you pass, you progress to a Legacy FundedNext Account where you can withdraw Performance Rewards.

Is there a Consistency Rule in the Legacy Challenge?

Yes. The Consistency Rule applies throughout the Challenge Phase. Your profit on any single day cannot exceed 40% of your total profit target.

 

Formula: 40% × Profit Target = Daily Profit Threshold

 

If your profit on any single day exceeds this threshold, the total profit required to pass is recalculated:

 

Required Total Profit = Highest Daily Profit ÷ 40%

 

Example — $50,000 Legacy Challenge (Profit Target: $3,000)

Daily threshold: 40% × $3,000 = $1,200 — keep daily profit below this.

If you earn $1,500 in a day: $1,500 ÷ 0.40 = $3,750. You would now need $3,750 total to pass, instead of $3,000.

The Consistency Rule encourages steady, repeatable profitability rather than relying on a single high-profit day.

 

🔗 See: Is there any consistency rule to be followed in the FundedNext Futures Challenge & FundedNext Account?

What is the Maximum Loss Limit in the Legacy Challenge?

Is there a daily loss limit in the Legacy Challenge?

No. The Legacy Challenge has no daily loss limit at any stage, giving you more flexibility in trade management. The Maximum Loss Limit remains your primary risk guardrail.

 

What trading rules must I follow in the Legacy Challenge?

You must follow all prohibited strategy rules throughout the Legacy Challenge to maintain disciplined and ethical trading. Breaking any of these can result in a breach.

 

🔗 See: What are the prohibited trading strategies of FundedNext Futures?

 

What is the Micro-Scalping policy for the Legacy Challenge Account?

Micro-scalping is opening and closing trades within 10 seconds to capture small, rapid price movements. Scalping is valid, but a high concentration of these trades affects trading consistency, so FundedNext Futures monitors a Micro-Scalping threshold across all account types.

 

During the Challenge Phase:

The Micro-Scalping percentage is the share of your total recorded profit from trades closed within 10 seconds, evaluated per cycle.

Only profitable trades count — you can close losing trades any time without affecting this rule.

At 30%, you receive a compliance warning (no penalty).

At 40% or above, your ability to reach the profit target and advance is placed on hold; it resumes automatically once your percentage drops back below 40%.

🔗 See: What is the Micro-Scalping policy in FundedNext Futures?

 

Is there a time limit to pass the Legacy Challenge?

No. There is no time limit — take as long as you need to reach your profit target while following the rules.

 

What happens after I pass the Legacy Challenge?

Once you meet the profit target while satisfying the Consistency Rule and all trading rules, you move to a Legacy FundedNext Account, where you can withdraw Performance Rewards.

To withdraw a Performance Reward, you need 5 Benchmark Days and $500 profit in the cycle. You earn an 80% Reward Share, withdraw a minimum of $250 (up to 50% of profit, capped by size), and after 30 Benchmark Days you unlock 100% withdrawals. You can earn Rising Trader, Champion Trader, and Limitless Trader certificates.

A Performance Reward is your share of the profits you earn for your skill and effort while trading a FundedNext Account after passing the Legacy Challenge. (At FundedNext Futures, what other firms call a "payout" is called a Performance Reward.) Here are all the rules that apply once you're funded.

 

Is there a Consistency Rule on the Legacy FundedNext Account?

No. Unlike the Challenge Phase, there is no Consistency Rule on the Legacy FundedNext Account. You have full flexibility in how much you earn on any given day.

How much can I withdraw, and how often, from the Legacy FundedNext Account?

Before completing 30 Benchmark Days, you can withdraw up to 50% of your accumulated profit per cycle, capped by size ($3,000 / $6,000 / $6,000), with a $250 minimum and at least $500 profit in the current cycle.

 

After 30 Benchmark Days, both the 50% limit and the cap are removed — you can withdraw up to 100% of your simulated profit.

 

Important: Withdrawing all of your simulated profit in a single request causes a hard breach.

 

🔗 See: What is a soft breach and a hard breach in FundedNext Futures?

 

What is my Reward Share from the Legacy FundedNext Account?

🔗 See: What will be my Reward Share from the Futures FundedNext Account?

 

What is the Legacy FundedNext Account withdrawal journey?

Trade and accumulate at least 5 Benchmark Days and $500 profit in the cycle.

Request a withdrawal (minimum $250, up to 50% of profit capped by size), receiving an 80% Reward Share.

Your first withdrawal resets the MLL to your initial balance.

Continue building Benchmark Days. Once you reach 30 Benchmark Days, the 50% limit and cap are removed, unlocking 100% withdrawals for all future cycles.

Unlike the other models, the Legacy FundedNext Account is not concluded after 5 Performance Rewards — the 30-Benchmark-Day milestone unlocks full withdrawals and you can continue trading.

All prohibited strategy rules continue to apply on your Legacy FundedNext Account, just as during the Challenge Phase. Breaking any of these can result in a breach.

 

🔗 See: What are the prohibited trading strategies of FundedNext Futures?

 

What is the Micro-Scalping policy for the Legacy FundedNext Account?

Micro-scalping is opening and closing trades within 10 seconds to capture small, rapid price movements. FundedNext Futures monitors a Micro-Scalping threshold across all account types.

 

On your FundedNext Account:

The Micro-Scalping percentage is the share of your total recorded profit from trades closed within 10 seconds, evaluated per cycle.

Only profitable trades count — you can close losing trades any time without affecting this rule.

At 30%, you receive a compliance warning (no deduction).

At 40% or above, the Micro-Scalping portion of your profit for that cycle is deducted in full. Your account is never terminated for micro-scalping, and future micro-scalping profit is subject to the same ongoing deduction.

If that deduction equals or exceeds your net profit for the cycle, no Performance Reward is issued and withdrawal is disabled for that cycle. A full breakdown appears in your dashboard.

🔗 See: What is the Micro-Scalping policy in FundedNext Futures?

 

How do I request my Performance Reward from the Legacy FundedNext Account?

Once you've met all the eligibility criteria, you can request your Performance Reward at the end of the trading day by transferring your profits to your wallet.

Please note: placing a trade on the same day removes the transfer-to-wallet option for that day. So if you intend to request your Performance Reward, do it on a day when you haven't opened a new trade — otherwise you'll need to wait until the next eligible day to transfer.

What is the Micro-Scalping policy for the Rapid Pro Challenge Account?

Micro-scalping is opening and closing trades within 10 seconds to capture small, rapid price movements. Scalping is valid, but a high concentration of these trades affects trading consistency, so FundedNext Futures monitors a Micro-Scalping threshold across all account types.

The Micro-Scalping percentage is the share of your total recorded profit from trades closed within 10 seconds, evaluated per cycle.

Only profitable trades count — you can close losing trades any time without affecting this rule.

At 30%, you receive a compliance warning (no penalty).

At 40% or above, your ability to reach the profit target and advance is placed on hold; it resumes automatically once your percentage drops back below 40%.

TL;DR: To pass the Rapid Daily Challenge, you must reach the profit target for your account size while respecting the daily loss limit, the Maximum Loss Limit, and all trading rules. There is no Consistency Rule at any stage, so you can hit the target in a single day or across multiple days. The daily loss limit is 500(25K), 1,000(50K), 1,250(100K), and the MLL is $1,000 / $2,000 / $2,500 on a Trailing End-of-Day basis. There is no time limit to pass.

What is the FundedNext Futures Rapid Daily Challenge?

The Rapid Daily Challenge is one of two paths in the Rapid Pro & Daily model, built for speed and simplicity. A daily loss limit acts as a guardrail throughout your journey, and there's no Consistency Rule at any stage. Once you pass, you progress to a Rapid Daily FundedNext Account where you can withdraw Performance Rewards daily using the buffer rule.

Is there a Consistency Rule in the Rapid Daily Challenge?

No. The Consistency Rule does not apply at any stage of the Rapid Daily path — neither in the Challenge Account nor the FundedNext Account. You can meet the profit target in a single day or across multiple days.

What trading rules must I follow in the Rapid Daily Challenge?

You must follow all prohibited strategy rules throughout the Rapid Daily Challenge to maintain disciplined and ethical trading. Breaking any of these can result in a breach.

 

🔗 See: What are the prohibited trading strategies of FundedNext Futures?

 

What is the Micro-Scalping policy for the Rapid Daily Challenge Account?

Micro-scalping is opening and closing trades within 10 seconds to capture small, rapid price movements. Scalping is valid, but a high concentration of these trades affects trading consistency, so FundedNext Futures monitors a Micro-Scalping threshold across all account types.

 

During the Challenge Phase:

The Micro-Scalping percentage is the share of your total recorded profit from trades closed within 10 seconds, evaluated per cycle.

Only profitable trades count — you can close losing trades any time without affecting this rule.

At 30%, you receive a compliance warning (no penalty).

At 40% or above, your ability to reach the profit target and advance is placed on hold; it resumes automatically once your percentage drops back below 40%.

🔗 See: What is the Micro-Scalping policy in FundedNext Futures?

 

Is there a time limit to pass the Rapid Daily Challenge?

No. There is no time limit — take as long as you need to reach your profit target while following the rules.

 

What happens after I pass the Rapid Daily Challenge?

Once you meet the profit target while following the daily loss limit, Maximum Loss Limit, and all trading rules, you move to a Rapid Daily FundedNext Account, where you can withdraw Performance Rewards daily using the buffer rule.

Is there a Consistency Rule in the Flex Challenge?

Yes. The Consistency Rule applies throughout the Challenge Phase. Your profit on any single day cannot exceed 40% of your total profit target.

 

Formula: 40% × Profit Target = Daily Profit Threshold

 

If your profit on any single day exceeds this threshold, the total profit required to pass is recalculated:

 

Required Total Profit = Highest Daily Profit ÷ 40%

 

Example — $50,000 Flex Challenge (Profit Target: $2,500)

Daily threshold: 40% × $2,500 = $1,000 — keep daily profit below this.

If you earn $1,500 in a day: $1,500 ÷ 0.40 = $3,750. You would now need $3,750 total to pass, instead of $2,500.

The Consistency Rule encourages steady, repeatable profitability rather than relying on a single high-profit day.

 

🔗 See: Is there any consistency rule to be followed in the FundedNext Futures Challenge & FundedNext Account?

It stops trailing and locks once your balance reaches the lock point for your size ($50,100 / $100,100 / $150,100).

Is there a daily loss limit in the Flex Challenge?

No. The Flex Challenge has no daily loss limit at any stage, giving you more flexibility in trade management. The Maximum Loss Limit remains your primary risk guardrail.

You must follow all prohibited strategy rules throughout the Flex Challenge to maintain disciplined and ethical trading. Breaking any of these can result in a breach.

 

🔗 See: What are the prohibited trading strategies of FundedNext Futures?

 

What is the Micro-Scalping policy for the Flex Challenge Account?

Micro-scalping is opening and closing trades within 10 seconds to capture small, rapid price movements. Scalping is valid, but a high concentration of these trades affects trading consistency, so FundedNext Futures monitors a Micro-Scalping threshold across all account types.

 

During the Challenge Phase:

The Micro-Scalping percentage is the share of your total recorded profit from trades closed within 10 seconds, evaluated per cycle.

Only profitable trades count — you can close losing trades any time without affecting this rule.

At 30%, you receive a compliance warning (no penalty).

At 40% or above, your ability to reach the profit target and advance is placed on hold; it resumes automatically once your percentage drops back below 40%.

🔗 See: What is the Micro-Scalping policy in FundedNext Futures?

No. There is no time limit — take as long as you need to reach your profit target while following the rules.

Once you meet the profit target while satisfying the Consistency Rule and all trading rules, you move to a Flex FundedNext Account, where you can withdraw Performance Rewards.

Is there any Consistency Rule in the FNL: 001 NO DLL 1-Step CFDs 50K Account?
July 22, 2026

TL;DR: The 40% Consistency Rule ensures your trading is stable and repeatable. No single trading day's profit cannot exceed 40% of your total profit target. If it does, your account is not breached — instead, your total profit target automatically increases to bring that day back within the 40% ratio.

What is the 40% Consistency Rule?

The rule requires that no single trading day's profit does not make up more than 40% of your overall profit target. It is designed to encourage steady, disciplined trading habits.

Does the consistency rule apply to both the Challenge Phase and the FundedNext Phase?

There is a consistency rule for the FNL: 001 NO DLL 1-Step CFDs 50K Challenge Phase. However, there is no consistency rule for the FNL: 001 NO DLL 1-Step CFDs 50K FundedNext Phase .

How is the daily profit limit calculated?

On a standard $50,000 account, your initial profit target is $3,000.

To find your daily profit limit, multiply the target by 40%.

Daily Profit Limit: $3,000 x 40% = $1,200.

As long as your daily profits stay at or below $1,200, your account maintains the consistency rule and your target stays at $3,000.

What happens if I make more than required profit in a single day?

If you make a larger profit than the required profit, you do not fail the Challenge Phase. Instead, your overall profit target scales up to keep that large trading day mathematically aligned with the 40% rule.

Your new required target is calculated by dividing your highest profit day by 40% ($0.40).

Outcome: Eligible. You can request up to $500. Based on your 80% profit split, you will receive $400 as your performance reward ($500 requested × 80%).

Benchmark Days: 3 Days (Fails the requirement of at least 5 Benchmark Days)

Outcome: Not Eligible. Even though you met the total profit threshold, you did not complete the required 5 Benchmark Days. You must complete 2 more Benchmark Days before submitting a request.

Withdrawal Limits: $200 is below the minimum $250 withdrawal limit.

What is a Benchmark Day and how does it work?

A Benchmark Day is a trading day where you successfully hit a specific minimum profit target based on closed trades, and profit is attributed to the day the trade closes, regardless of when it was opened. Benchmark Day is used to track your eligibility for the Performance Reward.

Requirements: For a $50K account, a Benchmark Day requires a net profit of at least $200 from closed trades.

Challenge Phase vs. FundedNext Phase: There are no Benchmark Day requirements while you are in the Challenge Phase. They only apply once you graduate to the FundedNext Phase.

Withdrawal Requirement: You must complete a minimum of 5 Benchmark Days within a single trading cycle to become eligible for a withdrawal.

Understanding the End-of-Day (EOD) Trailing Maximum Loss Limit for the FNL: 001 NO DLL 1-Step CFDs 50K Challenge Account
July 22, 2026

TL;DR: The Maximum Loss Limit (MLL) is the total amount you can lose before your account is breached. Rather than tracking losses in real-time, the EOD trailing system calculates your loss limit based on your highest closed account balance at the end of each trading day. Once your account balance reaches $52,100 or higher, the MLL permanently locks at $50,100 and will not trail upward again.

What is an End-of-Day (EOD) Trailing Maximum Loss Limit?

The Maximum Loss Limit (MLL) protects the account from major drawdowns. "End-of-Day Trailing" means your loss floor is not tied to real-time, floating equity during the trading session. Instead, the floor adjusts at the end of each trading day based on that day’s highest closed balance.

What is the baseline floor for a $50K account?

On a $50,000 account size, you have a $2,000 Maximum Loss Limit.

Starting Loss Limit: When you first open the account, your minimum allowed balance is $48,000 ($50,000 - $2,000).

How does the trailing loss work?

Let's look at how the maximum loss limit shifts day-by-day based on your trading performance:

Day 1 (Profitable Day):

You start at $50,000 and close the day with a $1,000 profit, making your balance $51,000.

Calculation: $51,000 - $2,000 = $49,000.

Result: Your new loss floor moves up to $49,000.

Day 2 (Hitting the Lock Zone):

You earn another $1,100, bringing your total balance to $52,100.

Calculation: $52,100 - $2,000 = $50,100.

Result: Because the calculation reaches $50,100 (initial balance + $100), the Maximum Loss Limit is permanently locked here. It will never trail any higher, even if your account continues to grow.

Day 3 (A Losing Day):

Your balance drops by $600, bringing your account down to $51,500.

Result: The MLL does not move down. It stays safely locked at $50,100.

Day 4 (Massive Growth Day):

Your balance jumps up by $3,500, hitting a high of $55,000.

Result: Because the floor is locked, the MLL remains exactly at $50,100. You now effectively have a much larger buffer ($4,900 of drawdown room) because your floor stopped trailing upward.

What happens to the MLL when I take my first Performance Reward?

If you request a withdrawal and your loss limit hasn't reached the lock zone yet (meaning it is still below $50,100), the first withdrawal will automatically bring and permanently lock your MLL floor at $50,100.

What is a Profitable Day and how does it work?

A Profitable Day is a trading day where your closed trades generate a net profit that meets or exceeds the minimum profit target. Profit is attributed to the day the trade closes, regardless of when it was opened.

 

Minimum requirement: On a $25,000 account, a Profitable Day requires at least $250 in net profit from closed trades ($25,000 × 1%).

 

Challenge Phase: Profitable Days count toward passing each phase.

News trading is not allowed on the FNL:002 12% MLL 3-Day Payout 2-Step 25K Challenge. If a trade is flagged as news trading, 100% of the profit from that trade is deducted from your account as a rule violation.

How are the Daily Loss Limit (DLL) and Maximum Loss Limit (MLL) calculated on the FNL:002 12% MLL 3-Day Payout 2-Step 25K Challenge?
August 4, 2026

TL;DR: Daily Loss Limit = Initial Balance x 4%, and Maximum Loss Limit = Initial Balance x 12%, calculated the same way as FundedNext's Stellar 2-Step Challenge. Both limits are based on your $25,000 initial balance, and any profit you bank before the limit is checked increases how much you're allowed to lose at that point, in both the Challenge Phase and on the FundedNext Account.

 

How do I calculate my Daily Loss Limit (DLL)?

Formula: Daily Loss Limit = Initial Balance x Daily Loss Limit Percentage (4%)

 

Swap charges, commissions, and fees are included in this calculation. Exceeding your Daily Loss Limit breaches your account.

Example 1: With no profit yet that day:

$25,000 × 4% = $1,000 Daily Loss Limit

 

Example 2: If you have made $500 in profit during the day:

$1,000 + $500 = $1,500 Daily Loss Limit

 

Losing more than $1,500 on closed or running trades that day would breach your Daily Loss Limit.

Your Daily Loss Limit resets every day at 00:00 (server time). Once it resets, the previous day's profit no longer counts, and your Daily Loss Limit returns to being purely a percentage of your initial balance: $25,000 x 4% = $1,000.

 

Here is a demonstration of how daily loss limit calculation works.

How do I calculate my Maximum Loss Limit (MLL)?

Formula: Maximum Loss Limit = Initial Balance x Maximum Loss Limit Percentage (12%)

Example 1: On a $25,000 FNL:002 12% MLL 3-Day Payout 2-Step 25K Challenge account: $25,000 x 12% = $3,000

Your account balance/equity must never drop below $25,000 minus $3,000 = $22,000. Dropping below this floor at any point, in the Challenge Phase or on the FundedNext Account, is a permanent breach of the account.

 

Example 2: If you make $1,000 profit, your Maximum Loss Limit increases to $3,000 + $1,000 = $4,000. You can now sustain a total loss of $4,000 from your original $25,000 balance, since your equity floor still sits at $22,000. The $22,000 floor itself does not move; it's the dollar amount you're allowed to lose from your current position that grows as your profit grows.

Here is an article explaining how the maximum loss limit is calculated.

If either limit is exceeded, the account will be considered breached or violated. You can find more details on this here.

 

Important note regarding server time

FundedNext's server follows a seasonal time adjustment: GMT+3 during Daylight Saving Time (typically the summer months) and GMT+2 for the rest of the year. Your Daily Loss Limit resets at 00:00 server time under this schedule.

What is the Perpetual Consistency Rule and how does it work?
September 8, 2026

TL;DR: The Perpetual Consistency Rule keeps your profits steady rather than reliant on one big day. The rule is simple: your highest single trading day ever recorded on the account must stay at 20% or less of your current cycle's total profit. What makes it perpetual is that your best-day record carries forward across every withdrawal cycle, as it stays with you until you beat it, at which point the new, bigger day becomes your record. As your profit grows, your best day becomes a smaller share of the total, so the rule only gets easier the more you trade. 

What is the Perpetual Consistency Rule? 

The Perpetual Consistency Rule is a Performance Reward condition on the FundedNext Futures FNL:003 50K Instant Account that requires your profits come from consistent, repeatable trading rather than a single outsized session. In one line: your best-ever trading day on the account can't be more than 20% of your current cycle's total profit (a cycle being the period since your last withdrawal, or since account start).

 

The word "perpetual" is what sets this rule apart. On most models, a consistency rule looks only at the cycle directly in front of it. Here, your highest trading day is remembered throughout the account lifespan. Once you record a best day, that figure follows you from cycle to cycle and becomes the number every future cycle is measured against, until you record an even bigger day, which then becomes your new benchmark.

 

Importantly, you are always in control of this rule. You're never penalized for having a strong day; a bigger day simply raises your benchmark. And because a growing cycle total makes any single day a smaller percentage of the whole, staying compliant becomes easier the longer you trade steadily.

 

How does the Perpetual Consistency Rule work? 

To check whether any cycle is consistent, take your highest recorded day and ask a single question: is it 20% or less of the cycle's total profit? If your total is high enough that your best day fits under that 20% ceiling, the cycle is consistent.

Finding the minimum total you need is just the reverse of taking 20%. Your total has to be large enough that your highest day lands at exactly 20% of it, which means your cycle total must be at least 5× your best day.

 

Example, a $500 best day needs a cycle total of at least $2,500 ($500 ÷ $2,500 = 20%) to be consistent.

How the rule works in your favor

The Perpetual Consistency Rule is designed to reward steady, repeatable trading, and it tends to fade into the background for consistent traders over time. Because your best day becomes a smaller and smaller share of your total as you keep earning, the more you trade consistently, the less the rule constrains you. You're never punished for a strong session, as a new personal best simply becomes your new mark to maintain.

What is the Perpetual Consistency Rule?

The Perpetual Consistency Rule ensures your profits remain steady and not dependent on a single big trading day. Your highest single trading day profit, ever recorded across all your withdrawal cycles, must stay at 20% or less of your current cycle's total profit.

What makes it perpetual is that your best-day record carries forward across every withdrawal cycle until you beat it. As your total profit grows, your best day becomes a smaller and smaller share of it, so the rule only gets easier the more you trade.

Setting Your Mark — First Cycle

Your first cycle is where you set your benchmark. Keep your best single trading day at 20% or less of your total cycle profit. Spread your gains across the cycle instead of relying on one big session, and you are set.

Example: Your highest day is $500. For that day to sit at 20% of the total, your cycle profit must reach at least $2,500. If your total for the cycle is $2,500 or more, consistency is met and that $500 day carries forward as your all-time record.

Keeping Your Mark — Later Cycles

Your best day stays on record after your first withdrawal. In each new cycle, keep that best-day figure at 20% or less of the new cycle's profit. The same $2,500 minimum applies until a bigger day is recorded.

 

Raising Your Mark

If you have a bigger day than your previous record, that day becomes your new all-time best. You are never penalized for a strong session. However, the minimum cycle profit required to stay consistent increases accordingly.

Example: You record a $600 day in Cycle 3. The new minimum cycle profit required is 3,000 (600 is 20% of $3,000). This $3,000 minimum now applies to every future cycle until an even bigger day is recorded.

Even if a single trade accounts for 50% or more of your total profit when the profit target hits, you will have until the end of the server day to generate additional profit and bring that trade's contribution below 50% of your total profit. However, if a single trade still accounts for 50% or more of your total profit at the end of the server day, your challenge will fail.

 

This rule ensures that a pass reflects consistent trading across multiple positions rather than one outsized winner.

 

Example

Best Trade Rule Failed: A single trade accounts for 50% or more of the total profit at the end of the server day.

Best Trade Rule Met: Additional profit is generated, bringing the contribution of the highest-profit trade below 50% of the total profit by the end of the server day.

TL;DR: If your 2FA code isn’t working, first ensure you are entering it quickly, as codes refresh every 30 seconds. Always use your authenticator app (like Google Authenticator) instead of searching for codes in your email, since email codes are not valid for 2FA login.

If issues continue, try resetting and reconfiguring your authenticator app by removing old entries and initiating a fresh 2FA setup with the new QR code. You can also clear your browser’s cache and cookies, switch to a different browser, or even log in from another device to isolate the problem.

 

If none of these steps resolve the issue, remove FundedNext 2FA from your authenticator app and re-add it following the correct process.

 

If you're experiencing trouble while using Two-Factor Authentication (2FA), here are some recommended steps to help resolve the issue:

 

Why is the 2FA code not working?

There could be several reasons your 2FA code isn’t working properly. Here are some steps to troubleshoot:

 

Enter the Code Quickly

2FA codes refresh every 30 seconds. Please make sure to enter the code promptly before it expires.

 

Use the Authenticator App, Not Email

Many traders mistakenly search for codes in their email. Please only use the code from your authenticator app (like Google Authenticator), as email codes are not valid for 2FA login.

 

Reset and Reconfigure the Authenticator App

If the code still doesn’t work, try this:

Remove all existing entries related to our platform from your authenticator app.

Log in to your account again and initiate a fresh 2FA setup using the new QR code provided.

This ensures that your device is properly synced with our system.

Clear Your Browser’s Cache and Cookies

Sometimes, saved data in your browser can cause login issues. Try clearing your cache and cookies before retrying.

 

Try a Different Browser

If the problem continues, switching to another browser might help isolate the issue.

 

Use a Different Device

If none of the above steps work, please try logging in from another device to see if the issue persists.

 

 

 

How to remove FundedNext 2FA from your Authenticator App?
Step 1: Open Your Authenticator App

Launch the app you currently use for 2FA (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Authy, etc.).

 

 

Step 2: Find the FundedNext Entry

Scroll through your list of accounts and look for any entries labeled “FundedNext.” It should be like this: "FundedNext: your email address."

 

 

Step 3: Delete/Remove the Entry

Tap and hold (or swipe left/right) on the FundedNext entry.

You will notice the option to remove the account.

Confirm the removal.

 

 

Step 4: Double-Check

Make sure no other FundedNext-related entries remain in your authenticator app.

For better visualization, here is a short video:

If you've tried all the above steps and still can't access your account, please reach out to our support team for further assistance. We're here to help!

Embed Video

 

​​Note: 2FA can only be disabled once. Once it's turned off manually for you, it cannot be disabled again in the future.
